record.original_question: Given two polytopes P and Q, determine when there exists a polytope whose facets are each isomorphic to either P or Q, and determine when such a polytope can be finite.

evidence.quote: Problem 19. Given two polytopes P and Q, when is there a polytope whose facets are each isomorphic to P or Q? When is there a finite such polytope?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope is a ranked partially ordered set (with a minimum and maximum element) satisfying the standard diamond and strong flag-connectedness conditions; its facets are the elements of co-rank 1, regarded together with their lower sections as abstract polytopes one rank lower. Two facets are isomorphic if there is a rank- and order-preserving bijection between the corresponding sections.

Given two abstract polytopes P and Q, give necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of an abstract polytope R such that every facet of R is isomorphic to either P or to Q (with both isomorphism types occurring). Moreover, characterize those pairs (P, Q) for which such an R can be chosen to have only finitely many faces.
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears as one of the open problems in a 2016/2018 list of open problems on k-orbit abstract polytopes. No subsequent paper resolving the general "mixed-facet" existence question for arbitrary pairs (P, Q) was located, so the problem appears to remain open.
